sn48.50:1.2: Aṅga was the country to that controlled the Ganges to the east of both Magadha and Vesālī. The market town of Āpaṇa was evidently the chief settlement of the region. At [mn54:1.2]() it was said to a town of the Aṅguttarāpans, in reference to the region of Aṅga north of both the Ganges and the Mahī, “Aṅga North of the Water”.
sn48.50:5.6: This is a unique description of the wisdom faculty.
